docs.title: openalex-snapshot Documentation
docs.text:
This folder contains internet-facing documentation for openalex-snapshot.

Argument precedence (highest wins): CLI arguments > config subcommand section > config defaults section > built-in defaults.

OpenAlex now publishes the snapshot natively in parquet, so openalex-snapshot is a parquet-native pipeline: download → verify_download → (auto) enrich → index → extract.

Recommended page order:

  1. quickstart.md
  2. commands/check.md
  3. commands/config.md
  4. commands/all.md
  5. commands/download.md
  6. commands/verify_download.md

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: OpenAlex now publishes the snapshot natively in parquet, so the flow is: download → verify_download → (auto) enrich → index → extract.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
cd openalex-snapshot
cargo build --release
./target/release/openalex-snapshot --help

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
./target/release/openalex-snapshot check \
  --root-dir /Volumes/openalex \
  --dataset all

docs.title: Download the parquet snapshot
docs.text:
Syncs the official parquet per-dataset into <root>/parquet/ and auto-enriches works (works_aws/ → works/, adding abstract + citation). Pass --no-enrich to skip.

./target/release/openalex-snapshot download --root-dir /Volumes/openalex

docs.title: Verify the download
docs.text:
Checks every file against the published manifest.json (presence + size + row count).

./target/release/openalex-snapshot verify_download --root-dir /Volumes/openalex
# fast size-only:  --quick      full row scan:  --full

docs.title: Enrich works (only if you used --no-enrich)
docs.text: ./target/release/openalex-snapshot enrich --root-dir /Volumes/openalex

docs.title: Build and verify indexes
docs.text:
./target/release/openalex-snapshot index \
  --root-dir /Volumes/openalex \
  --dataset all          # builds an index per dataset; skips the raw works_aws/ staging dir

./target/release/openalex-snapshot verify_index \
  --root-dir /Volumes/openalex \
  --dataset all

docs.title: Extract by IDs
docs.text:
./target/release/openalex-snapshot extract \
  --root-dir /Volumes/openalex \
  --ids /Volumes/openalex/ids.csv \
  --output /Volumes/openalex/extract.parquet

docs.title: Or run the whole pipeline from config
docs.text: ./target/release/openalex-snapshot all --config ./openalex-snapshot.yaml

docs.title: Download is slow or stalls
docs.text:
• Tune S3 transfer concurrency: --max-concurrent-requests, --max-queue-size, --multipart-chunksize (applied via a temporary AWS config, so your global ~/.aws/config is never modified).
  • Re-running download resumes incrementally — only missing/changed files are transferred.

docs.title: verify_download reports a size or row-count mismatch
docs.text: The local file no longer matches the published manifest.json. Re-run download to re-fetch the affected file(s), then re-run verify_download. Use --full for a row-scan that also catches corrupt data pages, or --quick to check presence + size only.

docs.title: index or extract can't find works
docs.text: extract routes W IDs to parquet/works/ (the enriched corpus). If you only downloaded the raw snapshot with --no-enrich, run enrich first (or re-run download without --no-enrich). index --dataset all deliberately skips the raw *_aws staging dirs.

docs.title: Out of memory
docs.text: The pipeline processes one parquet file at a time, so memory use is modest. If you still hit limits, constrain workers/memory: --workers <N> and --max-memory-mb <N>.

docs.title: Metadata layout
docs.text:
Current canonical location is openalex-snapshot_metadata/:

  • openalex-snapshot.lock — present while a command runs
  • reports/ — a JSON report per command, written only when failures occur
  • download/manifest.json — the fetched OpenAlex manifest (audit copy)
  • <dataset>/index/, <dataset>/index-verify/ — index logs

docs.title: Command: index
docs.text:
Build a parquet lookup index equivalent to R build_corpus_index().

Default dataset is all (build indexes for all datasets). Use --dataset <name> to limit to one dataset. When running with --dataset all, existing per-dataset index files are skipped and missing ones are built, and the raw *_aws staging dirs (e.g. works_aws) are skipped in favour of the canonical dataset (works). If --index-file is supplied, it is ignored in all mode.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
openalex-snapshot index \
  --root-dir /data \
  --dataset works

docs.title: Output columns
docs.text:
• id
  • id_block
  • parquet_file
  • file_row_number

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text: index reads the downloaded parquet corpus one file at a time, so its memory needs are modest — the default tuning is fine for any host with ≥4 GB RAM. Use --max-memory-mb <N> and --workers <N> only if you need to constrain resources.

docs.title: Command: all
docs.text: Run the full parquet-native pipeline from config.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: openalex-snapshot all --config ./openalex-snapshot.yaml

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. download (if enabled) — syncs the official parquet; auto-enriches works unless download.no_enrich: true
  2. verify_download (if enabled) — manifest presence/size/row-count
  3. index (if enabled) — builds <dataset>_id_idx.parquet for each dataset (skips *_aws)
  4. verify_index (if enabled)

Each stage can be toggled in the all: config section (enable_download, enable_verify_download, enable_index, enable_verify_index).

docs.title: check
docs.text: Run environment and capacity preflight checks before heavy operations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: openalex-snapshot check --root-dir . --dataset all

docs.title: What it checks
docs.text:
• dependency binaries (aws; DuckDB is no longer required — parquet I/O is pure Rust)
  • path writability for root/parquet/metadata
  • download disk requirement (parquet manifest.json size + safety margin)

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --strict fail on warnings as well as failures
  • --json machine-readable output
  • --precise enable precise source inventory estimate
  • shared runtime args: --dataset, --workers, --max-memory-mb

docs.title: Command: config
docs.text: Create or verify openalex-snapshot YAML config files.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
openalex-snapshot config --create complete
openalex-snapshot config --create safe --config ./openalex-snapshot-safe.yaml
openalex-snapshot config --verify --config ./openalex-snapshot.yaml

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• --create templates: complete (default), safe, fast
  • precedence: CLI > command section > defaults section > built-in defaults
  • --verify fails on unknown keys or wrong types

docs.title: Command: download
docs.text:
Download the OpenAlex snapshot, which is now published natively in parquet at s3://openalex/data/parquet/. No conversion is needed.

Each dataset is synced per-dataset so aws s3 sync --delete only ever manages its own directory:

  • works → <root>/parquet/works_aws/ (raw, the stable sync target)
  • every other dataset → <root>/parquet/<dataset>/

After a successful works sync, download auto-runs enrich to produce the canonical enriched <root>/parquet/works/ (raw columns + abstract + citation). Pass --no-enrich to skip enrichment (raw works_aws/ only).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
openalex-snapshot download --root-dir /data
# raw-only (skip enrichment):
openalex-snapshot download --root-dir /data --no-enrich
# one dataset:
openalex-snapshot download --root-dir /data --dataset authors

Per-dataset sync intent:

aws s3 sync --delete s3://openalex/data/parquet/<dataset>/ /data/parquet/<dataset>/ --no-sign-request

docs.title: Transfer tuning
docs.text:
These are applied via a temporary AWS_CONFIG_FILE for the sync only — your global ~/.aws/config is never modified:

Flag Default --max-concurrent-requests 10 --max-queue-size 50000 --multipart-chunksize 32MB

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The dataset list and disk-space preflight come from the published s3://openalex/data/parquet/manifest.json.
  • Validation is a separate step — run verify_download.
  • Space: delete parquet/works_aws/ to reclaim raw space (the next snapshot will re-download works in full, then re-enrich), or delete parquet/works/ (re-enrich anytime from works_aws/).

docs.title: Command: enrich
docs.text:
Enrich the raw works parquet with two derived columns, writing a separate enriched copy and leaving the downloaded data untouched:

  • <root>/parquet/works_aws/ — raw official works (input; manifest-verifiable)
  • <root>/parquet/works/ — enriched output (raw columns + abstract + citation)

download runs this automatically for works unless --no-enrich is given; the standalone command is for re-runs and repair.

docs.title: Derived columns
docs.text:
• abstract — plain text reconstructed from the JSON abstract_inverted_index (positions sorted ascending, words joined with single spaces).
  • citation — "Author (year)" / "A & B (year)" / "A et al. (year)" from authorships + publication_year; null year renders as (n.d.); null/empty authorships ⇒ null.

Each column is only added when its source column exists in the parquet.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
openalex-snapshot enrich --root-dir /data
# rebuild everything (ignore the incremental skip):
openalex-snapshot enrich --root-dir /data --overwrite

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Mirrors the updated_date=.../part_*.parquet partition layout.
  • Incremental: skips outputs newer than their source; re-running after an incremental download only rewrites changed partitions.
  • Row-parity self-check: the enriched row count must equal the source row count, or the file is treated as a failure and removed.
  • The raw works_aws/ is never modified, so it stays byte-identical to OpenAlex and the next snapshot's incremental aws s3 sync is unaffected.
  • Only the works dataset is supported (other datasets need no enrichment).

docs.title: Reading enriched works
docs.text: index --dataset all skips *_aws staging dirs and indexes the canonical works/; extract routes W IDs to works/, so extracted rows include abstract + citation.

docs.title: Command: extract
docs.text:
Extract records by OpenAlex IDs from CSV using per-dataset parquet indexes.

The command auto-routes each ID to a dataset using:

  • entity prefixes (W, A, S, I, T, K, P, F, G, C)
  • taxonomy namespaces (countries/, continents/, languages/, domains/, fields/, subfields/, sdgs/, work-types/, source-types/, licenses/, institution-types/)

It writes one output file per resolved dataset as:

  • <output_base>_<dataset>.parquet

Unknown/unmapped IDs are skipped and reported.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
openalex-snapshot extract \
  --root-dir /Volumes/openalex \
  --ids /Volumes/openalex/ids.csv \
  --output /Volumes/openalex/extract.parquet

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Requires per-dataset index files (for example parquet/works_id_idx.parquet).
  • Build indexes first with openalex-snapshot index.
  • Use --dataset <name> to restrict extraction to one dataset.

docs.title: Command: progress
docs.text: Monitor active/recent runs from report/log files, including from another terminal session.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
openalex-snapshot progress --root-dir /data
openalex-snapshot progress --root-dir /data --once
openalex-snapshot progress --root-dir /data --command index --dataset works

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• default mode is live watch
  • --once prints one snapshot and exits
  • --json emits machine-readable output

docs.title: Command: prune-reports
docs.text: Remove older report files and keep the latest set.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: openalex-snapshot prune-reports --root-dir /data

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• keeps recent reports and deletes older ones according to command policy
  • use before long-running batches to reduce metadata noise

docs.title: Command: report
docs.text: Show run reports written under openalex-snapshot_metadata/reports/. A report is written only when a command has failures.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# show latest reports with per-dataset breakdown (default)
openalex-snapshot report --root-dir /data --latest

# show only aggregate totals (suppress per-dataset rows)
openalex-snapshot report --root-dir /data --latest --summary

# show full JSON details
openalex-snapshot report --root-dir /data --latest --full

# filter by command
openalex-snapshot report --root-dir /data --command verify_download --latest

docs.title: Default output
docs.text:
Each report is shown as a header line followed by a per-dataset table:

=== verify_download [2026-06-27 00:28:53  3s  ok]  verify_download-1782660000.json
  dataset                scanned       ok   failed  skipped
  ------------------------------------------------------
  authors                    546      546        0        0
  works                     2127     2127        0        0  !

Datasets with failures are marked with !.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• --config is a global flag and must precede the subcommand: openalex-snapshot --config ./openalex-snapshot.yaml report
  • --summary prints only aggregate totals; suppresses per-dataset rows
  • --command <name> filters by command (e.g. download, verify_download, index)
  • --full prints full JSON details

docs.title: skills
docs.text: Create a project-local skills/ starter pack for AI coding agents.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: openalex-snapshot skills --root-dir .

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --root-dir <path> root containing snapshot/parquet/metadata layout
  • --overwrite rewrite generated template files
  • --stdout print template manifest/content
  • --explain print planned actions only

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Default mode is non-destructive: missing files are created, existing files are kept.
  • Generated content focuses on command operation, pipeline runbook, recovery, and docs hygiene.

docs.title: Command: verify_download
docs.text: Validate the downloaded parquet corpus against the official s3://openalex/data/parquet/manifest.json.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
openalex-snapshot verify_download --root-dir /data
# size-only (fastest):
openalex-snapshot verify_download --root-dir /data --quick
# full row scan (catches data-page corruption):
openalex-snapshot verify_download --root-dir /data --full

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
For every file listed in the manifest:

  • presence — the local file exists (works files are checked under works_aws/)
  • size — local byte size equals the manifest content_length
  • row count — parquet row count equals the manifest record_count
  • default (meta): footer metadata only (parquet_file_metadata) — cheap
  • --full: actual COUNT(*) scan — slower, catches corrupt data pages
  • --quick: skip the row-count check entirely
  • extra files (--check-extra, on by default) — flag local .parquet files not in the manifest

The enriched works/ directory is validated by enrich's own row-parity self-check, not here.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: A JSON report is written only when failures are detected; a clean run prints a one-line summary and exits 0.

docs.title: Command: verify_index
docs.text: Verify index integrity and coverage for one dataset or all datasets.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
openalex-snapshot verify_index \
  --root-dir /data \
  --dataset all

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• required index columns are present
  • referenced parquet files exist
  • row-number references are valid

docs.title: Runbook: Recovery and Resume
docs.text: The parquet-native pipeline is resumable at every stage — just re-run the command.

docs.title: Resume a download
docs.text:
aws s3 sync is incremental: re-running download only transfers files that are missing or changed. Auto-enrichment of works also resumes (see below).

openalex-snapshot download --root-dir /data

docs.title: Re-enrich works
docs.text:
enrich is incremental: it skips enriched files that are newer than their source and only rebuilds changed partitions. Force a full rebuild with --overwrite.

openalex-snapshot enrich --root-dir /data
openalex-snapshot enrich --root-dir /data --overwrite   # rebuild everything

If parquet/works/ is gone but parquet/works_aws/ is intact, just re-run enrich. If parquet/works_aws/ was deleted to save space, re-run download (works is re-fetched, then re-enriched).

docs.title: Rebuild an index
docs.text:
Per-file shard index building is resumable; --overwrite forces a clean rebuild.

openalex-snapshot index --root-dir /data --dataset all
openalex-snapshot index --root-dir /data --dataset works --overwrite

docs.title: Re-check integrity
docs.text:
openalex-snapshot verify_download --root-dir /data        # vs the published manifest
openalex-snapshot verify_index   --root-dir /data --dataset all

docs.title: Diagnose failures
docs.text:
A JSON report is written under openalex-snapshot_metadata/reports/ only when a command has failures:

  • openalex-snapshot report --root-dir /data --latest --full
  • openalex-snapshot progress --root-dir /data --once
